input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: Argument.get_help_record returns self.help unchanged, so the second element of the tuple is None for an undocumented argument even though format_arguments now feeds every record straight into formatter.write_dl without a fallback.
- failure path: A command declares two arguments and sets help on only one; running it with --help makes write_dl measure and wrap a None description and the help command crashes with a TypeError instead of printing usage.

Reviewer finding
- description: Undocumented arguments return `(metavar, None)` instead of `(metavar, "")`, causing help formatting to fail when documented and undocumented arguments are mixed.
- rationale: When a command has at least one argument with help text and another whose help is unset, the positional-arguments section passes both records to `formatter.write_dl`. The undocumented argument's description remains `None`, which fails when the formatter measures the table's string widths. Users requesting help get an exception instead of help output; the previous fallback supplied an empty string.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label. get_help_record returns None for help on an undocumented argument, that record is passed to write_dl together with a documented argument's record, and write_dl fails when it measures the None, so --help crashes.
